intro.text: Kronos Worldwide, Inc. (NYSE: KRO) (“Kronos”), incorporated in Delaware in 1989, is a leading global producer and marketer of value-added titanium dioxide pigments, or TiO 2 , a base industrial product used in a wide range of applications. We, along with our distributors and agents, sell and provide technical services for our products to approximately 3,000 customers in 100 countries with the majority of our sales in Europe, North America and the Asia Pacific region. We believe we have developed considerable expertise and efficiency in the manufacture, sale, shipment and service of our products in domestic and international markets. Effective July 16, 2024 (“Acquisition Date”), we acquired the 50% joint venture interest in Louisiana Pigment Company, L.P. (“LPC”) held by Venator Investments, Ltd. (“Venator”) for consideration of $185 million less a working capital adjustment.

lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Pension and retiree benefits
lines.why: Promised to employees for their work: operating (some analysts treat the unfunded part as debt).

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: We believe we are the largest TiO 2 producer and chloride process TiO 2 producer in Europe with 45% of our 2025 sales volumes attributable to markets in Europe.
Sales of our core TiO 2 pigments represented approximately 90% of our net sales in 2025.
Our TiO 2 business is enhanced by the following three complementary businesses, which comprised approximately 10% of our net sales in 2025:
We sell to a diverse customer base with no single customer representing 10% or more of our net sales in 2025.
Our largest ten customers accounted for approximately 35% of net sales in 2025.
In 2025, approximately 90% of our sales were attributable to sales of TiO 2 .
Revenue from non-U.S. markets accounted for approximately 66%, 66% and 64% of our revenue for the years ended December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively.
We sell TiO 2 to approximately 3,000 customers, with the top ten customers approximating 35 % in 2023, 39 % in 2024 and 35 % in 2025 of net sales.
One customer accounted for approximately 12 % of our net sales in 2023 and 10 % of our net sales in 2024.
We did not have sales to a single customer representing 10% or more of net sales in 2025.

We rely upon unpatented proprietary knowledge and continuing technological innovation and other trade secrets to develop and maintain our competitive position.
Our ability to make payments on and refinance our debt and to fund planned capital expenditures depends on our ability to generate cash flow in the future.

We rely on integrated information technology systems to manage, process and analyze data, including to facilitate the manufacture and distribution of products to and from our facilities, receive, process and ship orders, manage the billing of and collections from customers and manage payments to vendors.
Certain of our leases include variable lease payments that depend on a specified index or rate.
While our future global operations depend on a number of different factors, we do expect to have future U.S. inclusions in taxable income related to GILTI.
